body:
This article appeared on Signal, a capital markets news service, at 3:15 p.m. on Oct. 13, 2026.

The government will convene the National Pension Service's Fund Management Committee during the National Assembly's annual audit of government agencies, a move market participants described as unusual. The committee is expected to review the pension fund's July investment performance.

The NPS will hold a working-level performance review panel on Oct. 16 and the Fund Management Committee on Oct. 20, according to investment banking sources on the 13th. The schedule falls between a parliamentary audit of the NPS on Oct. 14 and a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Health and Welfare on Oct. 27. Committee meetings are typically held before or after the audit period, making the timing unusual.

Members are expected to examine the fund's July returns. The fund stood at 1,684 trillion won at the end of July, according to disclosures by the NPS Investment Management division, down 182 trillion won from 1,866 trillion won at the end of June. The overall return fell to 14.84% at the end of July from 27.22% at the end of June. Returns remain solid on a year-to-date basis, but officials inside and outside the NPS said extreme volatility in Korean equities in July dealt a direct blow to performance.

Some observers attribute the sharp decline in fund assets to a suspension of rebalancing. The NPS sets target weightings for each asset class, but the committee suspended their application early this year as domestic equities rallied.

The meeting marks the first official engagement for Lee Kyu-hong, the new chief investment officer who heads the NPS Investment Management division. Lee previously served as CIO of NH-Amundi Asset Management, chief executive of Ascendas Asset Management and CIO of the Korea Teachers Pension. Lee is seen as having built broad experience across asset allocation, alternative investments and risk management without concentration in any single asset class. While Lee is viewed as a fitting choice for the role, setting asset weightings is seen as among the most pressing tasks ahead. "With no other buyers stepping in unless pension funds move first, NPS rebalancing is expected to become a major issue going forward," an investment banking industry official said.
